I don't get what you're asking here, and I think you're just trying to set up a false dichotomy. "Insensitive" and "a right" aren't mutually exclusive. Both the Confederate Flag and a Satanic statue can easily be both.

The way I see it, the confederate flag is a symbol of slavery and racism (as well as other things; it is, of course, in the eye of the beholder). This is a pretty fair interpretation of the flag, as this was what the southern states fought for.

Symbols of Satanism are on the other hand controversial mostly because of what many Christians think of Satanism, not because the symbols in themselves carries a message of hate, racism, slavery or whatever. Quite contrary, it's more of a symbol of religious freedom, which is generally agreed to be a good thing, as long as people behave.

Of course, different people associate the symbols with different things, but from a secular standpoint with modern Western values of freedom, brotherhood and equality, it really makes sense for the confederate flag to be considered insensitive and bad, while satanic statues carries no such meanings, and can be considered a right from the standpoint of religious freedom.

I think these two things fall under two different categories really, but the main thing they share is where they are displayed.

We're supposed to have a secular government, so no government building or organization should be putting up religious icons. Since some of the more Christian areas have government buildings with things like the Ten Commandments up, all other religious have the right to request their icons to be displayed. Failure to do so would show government favoring a religion. Hence the recent ruling on why the Satanic Statue had a right to be displayed if the Ten Commandments were going to be displayed at the Oklahoma capitol.

For the confederate flag, you have an icon that many feel rallies the old teachings of the South. You can fly this flag on your own personal property all you want. The issue comes again under something being displayed on a government building. I don't think there's anything illegal about it, but it might be a bad idea if that's how you want to represent your local community. Like in South Park where they had that flag hanging a black man. Nothing illegal about it, but damned if you want that to represent who you are today.

It really depends on which type of alcohol you consumed as to whether you've been knocked out of keto or not. If it was a liqueur (usually flavored/sweetened) then that can/will absolutely knock you out. If it's something like whiskey (not flavored, just standard) then there are no carbs or sugar involved and that probably won't. It does have calories, though...so keep that in mind.
I limit my alcohol intake to distilled drinks, with no sugar/carb content. I have them several times a week for a few weeks, and then I'll go months without. In my experience, it's had no effect on my progress at all, but you have to figure out how your body reacts.

I found my desire for alcohol dropped significantly with keto. I used to drink on a fairly regular basis. I also had a pretty good tolerance. I don't know if it was because I went without while starting keto, or keto itself, but my tolerance dropped a lot. I also enjoy it less now.

I've had some bottles of wine and some liquor sitting around for a couple years now. I have no idea when I'll get around to consuming them.

All of that said, most alcohol has never kicked me out of ketosis. I'm a whisky and wine person. Those have never given me problems. Now, they would slow weight loss. That's not really a "problem" so much as an expected side effect.
